prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1132; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a hit while turning left at an intersection, with the other vehicle striking the rear quarter of the claimant's car. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all contact is being routed through the attorney's office going forward.

Entry 2: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement line up with the reported impact, and the damage on the claimant's vehicle is consistent with a side-to-rear collision of this kind. Two independent witnesses describe the same sequence of events.

Entry 3: Police records and the witnesses both place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. The driver is listed on the policy, and no earlier damage to the vehicle has come to light; nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 4: The claimant reports lower back strain and has been treating with a physician. The reported injury is a plausible result of a collision of this type, and there is no record of prior trouble in that body area.

Entry 5: Treatment has followed a typical course, with therapy visits tapering as the claimant's mobility and pain improved. Medical notes are consistent with the progress the claimant describes.

Entry 6: The claimant's account of the accident has stayed the same across every call, written statement and meeting with the adjuster, with no material differences in the details.

Entry 7: Based on the consistent evidence, the claim is moving forward on the liability and injury components, with counsel copied on the next status letter and a reserve review scheduled.
